Day 12,

With the toppling of Sunnyglade to the orcish horde, I had my doubts we would ever see it reclaimed as our own.

However, something seems to be driving them off. Something even the foul orcs fear.

Commander,

A decisive blow has been delivered to the growing Horde presence. 

Their training camps have been overrun, further diminishing their forces and allowing us to acquire much needed supplies for our brothers and sisters in arms.

Should we decide to take further action, I stand ready.

- Cornelius, Keeper of the Watch

Zizplink's Pick-Me-Up:

1. An Armful of Crawler Spittle
I don't know how much you can carry in your arms, but the more the merrier. Folks love bubbly drinks. Go get them from the crawlers along the beach.

2. A Bucket of Fresh Chum
This adds the rich meaty flavor to the drink! The local fish market probably has some extra. Try seeing if you can't buy some from them.

3. A Spoonful of Goblin Degreaser
Helps take the burn off. You should be able to get some from the engineers around town.

4. A Splash of Expired Poison
This ingredient is just for spite. But it's funny. The poison vendor in town should have a few bottles lying around.

texts.text: The calm comes before the storm.

<You touch the small white crystal and you can hear faint sounds on the wind. This is an audio recording of some sort.>

"An excerpt from the Shal'nan's speech at the groundbreaking ceremony for the Shrine of the Four Winds, Zephras Isle."

"With the founding of our new home here in the clouds, we embark on a new age of peace and prosperity for our people.

You have all endured so much to make it here. I have watched our people grow into a hardy, self-reliant society, which fills me with a pride I cannot hope to describe in full.

The greatest part of that pride, however, is that it has become clear to me that I no longer have any need to act as our singular ruler."

"Thus, I am abdicating my position as your leader and handing over governance of our Skyborne Isles to a carefully chosen council of provincial elders. After the transition period is over, you will have the opportunity to choose your own leaders, and your voices will determine the direction we take from here on. 

You have demonstrated the ability to lead yourselves better than any king, queen, prince, or other individual sovereign ever could--and that fills me with profound pride."

"I will continue to serve our people here on Zephras, and I will devote much of my time to furthering our relationship with the wind spirits to whom we owe so much. The elemental spirits are wondrous and wise, and we still have so much to learn from one another.

I am devoted to seeing the shen'dorei persevere in this beautiful and strange realm--and to seeing that we do so freely, justly, and unshackled by tyranny."

"Thank you for everything you've sacrificed, everything you've built, and everything you've taught me about how to be a better person. You all represent the unshakable resolve of the shen'dorei people. We will thrive in this beautiful new world and reach new heights together."

<You touch the small white crystal and you can hear faint sounds on the wind. This is an audio recording of some sort.>

"The Rebellion in Eldre'Thalas, Part 1"

"In the days immediately following the turmoil at the Well of Eternity, there was much unrest in Eldre'Thalas. The demonic forces that poured from the Well nearly overwhelmed the beleaguered elvish kingdoms, ravaging the land and killing indiscriminately. If not for the intervention of the demigod Goldrinn and the sacrifice of countless kaldorei heroes, the kingdom of Eldre'Thalas would surely have been overrun and destroyed."

"After the climax of the war and the Great Sundering of Kalimdor, the new reality of a world bereft of the sustaining magic on which our people depended quickly became apparent. The ruling house of Eldre'Thalas--House Tortheldrin--rapidly set plans in motion to ensure stability and continuity of our way of life. However, the methods they intended to employ left many deeply concerned."

"The young Prince Tortheldrin intended to build a network of crystalline foci and use them to siphon and shape a new font of power for our people to draw upon. The point of contention for many was that he intended to use the very power that nearly destroyed our world to accomplish this. He meant to siphon this power from a demon world within the Twisting Nether itself. 

Many rightly feared this could open a new door through which demonic entities might gain once again access to our world."

<You touch the small white crystal and you can hear faint sounds on the wind. This is an audio recording of some sort.>

"The Rebellion in Eldre'Thalas, Part 2"

"There were those who loudly opposed the Prince's plan to channel a font of demonic energy to power his network of crystalline foci. Many of the detractors were members of outspoken noble families who attempted to use their influence to turn public sentiment against House Tortheldrin and the Prince's plan."

"Prince Tortheldrin grew frustrated, fearing that delays and debate would lead to the further deterioration of his kingdom. 

As a result, his response to this resistance was swift and brutal. Over the course of a single bloody night, a purge was carried out that saw the complete destruction of dozens of noble houses. All who publicly opposed Tortheldrin were abruptly silenced, and entire lineages were destroyed overnight."

"The terror of such brazen suppression caused a shocked silence to fall over the people of Eldre'Thalas. All discourse around Prince Tortheldrin's plan abruptly ceased... for a time, at least. Unfortunately for the Prince, the harder tyrants squeeze their people, the brighter the flames of resistance burn.

There were those who resolved to ensure our people did not repeat Queen Azshara's mistakes. A group of scholars formerly of the order of the Shen'dralar met in secret and formed a pact. Swearing to stop the Prince by any means necessary, they began to plant the seeds of rebellion."

<You touch the small white crystal and you can hear faint sounds on the wind. This is an audio recording of some sort.>

"The Rebellion in Eldre'Thalas, Part 3"

"The leader of the rebels was a mysterious figure known only as the 'Shal'nan' or, 'The Veiled One.' He wore a featureless golden mask intended to conceal his identity and protect those close to him. This man quickly became a symbol for ordinary citizens who would stand up against oppression, and the word Shal'nan became a battle cry synonymous with rebellion.

Through sabotage, coercion, and--according to some rumors--assassination, the rebels quickly became a thorn in the side of Prince Tortheldrin's efforts to construct his network of crystalline foci."

"The message of resistance spread by the Shal'nan began to gain traction within Eldre'Thalas, due in no small part to the very public embarrassment the Prince suffered nearly daily at the hands of rebel operations.

Awareness of an alternative, more naturalistic way of life also spread quickly in the kingdom at this time. This was heavily influenced by the example set by the Cenarion druids, who had taken control of the greater kaldorei empire in the northern part of the continent. There were even rumors that the rebels were secretly supported by covert agents sent by the new de facto leader of the night elves: the Archdruid Malfurion Stormrage."

"The Prince railed against the idea of an alternative path to combat his people's dependence on magic. He claimed that calls to embrace naturalistic magic were propaganda spread by illegitimate usurpers to Queen Azshara's vacant throne. 

He and his supporters dismissed druidic magic as base and barbaric--utterly beneath the proud, ancient traditions of the highborne. Yet the practice of druidism began to take hold on the fringes of Eldre'Thalas society, and with it, the rebellion continued to grow."

<You touch the small white crystal and you can hear faint sounds on the wind. This is an audio recording of some sort.>

"The Rebellion in Eldre'Thalas, Part 4"

"On the eve of the planned summoning ritual, the Shal'nan and his forces struck. Seeing this as their final opportunity to thwart Prince Tortheldrin's reckless plan, they made a daring raid on the Prince's sanctum, intent on stopping the ritual.

Just as the Shal'nan and the rebels feared, the poorly considered spell spiraled out of control and threatened to destroy the entire city center. 

As the battle raged, wild magics tore through the streets, opening portals to the Nether itself and manifesting malevolent arcane monstrosities that preyed mercilessly upon the defenseless citizens of Eldre'Thalas."

"In the end, the worst of the destruction was narrowly avoided due to the rebels' intervention, but the price was steep. The battle claimed many lives on all sides, but the rebels suffered the greatest losses. 

The Shal'nan himself was the only one to survive the final confrontation within Tortheldrin's sanctum. Those closest to the Shal'nan have widely documented that whatever injury he suffered in that last battle left him forever changed. In the centuries since those dark days, the Shal'nan has never spoken of what occurred, and he becomes withdrawn and wistful when asked."

"In the immediate aftermath of the battle, Tortheldrin's forces were scattered and disorganized. Most were occupied with securing the city once more, and this distraction allowed the remaining rebels to escape and regroup. With nowhere else to go, the Shal'nan marched what was left of his exhausted forces west, toward the coast."

"When the beleaguered rebel army arrived at the port city of Eldre'narr, the magisters in control of the city had already heard of Tortheldrin's mighty rage--and of his standing order to kill any rebel found on sight. In an act of miraculous mercy, the magisters made no move to hinder the rebels' progress, allowing them to commandeer a number of ships without resistance.

The Shal'nan understood that this act of mercy would likely expose many in Eldre'narr to Tortheldrin's wrath. Even so, he accepted this unexpected gift with grace and, with a heavy heart, sailed his people west into the unknown."

<You touch the small white crystal and you can hear faint sounds on the wind. This is an audio recording of some sort.>

"The Sky-Touched Mystery"

"Much of the flora and fauna of the Skyborne Isles has been shaped by the elemental forces that reign here in the realm of Skywall. Many creatures once bound to the earth now bear avian traits such as beaks, talons, and feathers. Others have gained the power of flight, though such transformations remain less common than other outward changes.

Among the shen'dorei, the elemental plane's influence upon the body has been gradual and subtle. Yet in recent generations its effects have grown increasingly dramatic. Consider, for instance, the phenomenon now commonly called the "Sky-Touched Blessing."

"It's well documented since our ascent to Skywall that our people have adopted more lithe, slender forms, but this occurred over the course of many millennia. In contrast, the first recorded case of the Sky-Touched Blessing--which causes shen'dorei children to be born with vivid cerulean skin--was noted fewer than five generations ago.

Within a single generation of its first appearance, one child in twenty born among the Skyborne bore this curious alteration. Two generations later, that rate had doubled."

"Today, three in ten children born on the Skyborne Isles have the striking complexion of the Sky-Touched. In recent centuries, the acceleration of our physical alterations has increased, and many scholars believe that the last vestiges of our kaldorei heritage may vanish entirely within two to three more generations.

The cause of this transformation may never be fully understood. Yet it is plain that, in making our lives within the elemental plane, we as a people are being changed by it in turn. Skywall is a realm of wonders, but this serves as a sober reminder that we still know perilously little of what such a place may work upon those not born to it."

<You touch the small white crystal and you can hear faint sounds on the wind. This is an audio recording of some sort.>

"On The Windlord."

"Who is Al'Akir the Windlord? The priests of the radical Al'Aketh would have us believe him to be the true ruler of Skywall, the realm we now call home. In their telling, we are but interlopers here, and one day Al'Akir shall appear before us to reckon with our trespass into his dominion within the elemental plane.

Though such claims may at first seem the ravings of the misguided or the mad, there may yet be some measure of truth in them. When asked of Al'Akir's nature, the wind spirits grow evasive and agitated. Indeed, even the mere speaking of the so-called "Windlord's" name appears to cause them profound unease, perhaps even fear."

"Whatever the truth may be, our benefactors clearly have no wish to speak of Al'Akir or his servants, and they are quick to dismiss all rumors of the Windlord's presence as idle fancy, unworthy of serious heed. They assure us that we need not trouble ourselves with such matters here, safe upon our Skyborne Isles. While this offers solemn comfort to many, it also raises a troubling question: what, precisely, are the wind spirits concealing from us?"

"Of late, the magisters of the High Order have grown increasingly wary of the wind spirits' motives, insisting that all powers and perils native to this realm must be better understood. Even if such dangers lie far from us now, the magisters maintain that such knowledge will better prepare us to face whatever may yet come."

"The skyseer elders among the Windshapers, by contrast, place implicit trust in the wind spirits and regard any questioning of their designs as an affront to our benefactors. They hold that our patrons in Skywall have already sacrificed much to bring us here and sustain us. They assert that if any further knowledge was vital to our survival, they would surely reveal it in due course. This difference in belief has given rise to no small measure of tension between the two orders.

Whatever the truth may be, it is plain that we are not alone in this realm, and that many mysteries yet remain beyond our present understanding."

npc:11216.text: Hello young $g Master:Mistress;. I am Eva Sarkhoff and this is my husband, Lucien. It is a pleasure to make your acquaintance.

And go where? It was all that we knew; all that we had known and all that we would ever know.$B$BEventually, we lost contact with the Barovs and ultimately, were separated from the household. We knew not what happened to the other servants, only that there were screams. Tortured screams.$B$BKnowing that we had nowhere to go, Lucien and I were forced to hide in our quarters. During the day, when the school was relatively quiet, Lucien would sneak out to scrounge up food and drink.

Certainly, $g sir:miss;. We were once servants of the house Barov: What is now known as the Scholomance.$B$BI was the head maid and Lucien was Master Barov's butler.$B$BWe had worked for the Barovs for decades, until...$B$B<Eva weeps.>

Oh it's just so horrible, $g sir:miss;. The house Barov was once full of life... full of splendor. The manor was the Barov's primary residence amidst their far reaching empire.$B$BLucien and I noticed that as the days progressed, the Barovs became depressed. Despondent. Paranoia and rage often overcame the master and missus. At night, we could hear the Barovs arguing in their chambers. From what we understood, their greed had 'broken the dam,' so to speak.

Restraints? There are things in this world far more restraining than bars and shackles, young $g master:mistress;. The undead surrounded us, constantly tormenting us with horrifying acts of depravity.$B$BFinally, he came. He introduced himself as Doctor Theolen Krastinov. We came to know him as 'The Butcher.'

We did this for about six months and watched as the house went through horrifying changes. Foul monsters roamed through the manor at will. Dark cultists populated every inch with various paraphernalia relating to rituals and sacrifices. We knew that we could not hide much longer.$B$BAs expected, we were found and captured. They stripped us of all our clothes and laid us out inside a circle of blood. We sat there for days, naked and terrified.

We finally understood what the screams were from. The Butcher exposed us to pain that we did not know existed. He used us in countless experiments, attempting to devise a plague.$B$BThe days turned to weeks. We would have died on the first day had it not been for that cruel bastard keeping us alive through magical means.

We suspect that in order to preserve their fortune and hold of the land - well past their lifespan - the Barovs made a deal with a powerful human mage named Kel'Thuzad.$B$B<Eva shudders.>$B$BFrom this deal sprang the school of necromancy: A place which bore the Cult of the Damned and would become their capital.$B$BAs each week passed, the house Barov became more and more decrepit...$B$BDark beings began to take residence in the various wings of the house. Upkeep became impossible... and disgusting.

npc:251376.text:
The hunters and rangers of Zephras have never been more needed. The winds grow ever harsher, and the magic that sustains our island is fading. The wilds have never been more wild, and people like me are needed to keep our people safe.

npc:251684.text: H-Hello. You'll have to excuse me, I'm used to your kind running from me.
Oh, that's okay. I-I'll be here if you want to learn some other time. T-Thank you for talking to me!

Oh, these things? I built them. My little friends helped me. I'm not very good at remembering things, but, um, I do know that at one point I used to build a lot of things. Big things! But then, like I said... I was here. The things I build aren't so big and impressive anymore. Still makes me h-happy, heh.

B-but... If you want, I can show you how to build things too!

That is... a very good question. I have a hard time remembering things, but I do remember something... "Engineer", perhaps? I think that's what, or who, I was.

Other than that, all I can seem to remember is soaring through the sky, then seeing a flash of lightning before things got very bumpy. Then... a crash.

It's been... a long time though. A very long time.

npc:251968.text:
<Ayessa Dawnsinger eyes you with barely-contained fury.> 

You are either very bold, or very stupid to so brazenly step foot into our domain after spilling Windshaper blood. We are slow to forgive, and we never forget. 

You should remove yourself from here at once. If we weren't in the center of Zephras, you would already be dead.

Hmm, I see. Very well then, $c. The Windshapers will provide aid. Please inform Valennia that she can count on us for this fight.

<Ayessa lowers her voice dangerously.> 

Do not mistake our cooperation for any sort of forgiveness. You owe the Windshapers blood, and someday we will collect.

npc:252373.text: The followers of the old Highborne ways have never been more hungry to gain knowledge and reclaim what we've lost. If you would seek to wield the power of the arcane and have the aptitude, I can help you take your next steps.

npc:252380.text: Welcome to my shop; it's good to see another Tailor here in Valanaar. Are you here for a lesson perhaps?

npc:252383.text:
The Peacekeepers can't hope to muster the numbers needed for an outright assault on the shrine. Without the Windshapers and the High Order bolstering our numbers, we stand no chance. They both pledged their aid when we need it. Now is the time.

Unfortunately, some recent events have led to outright bloodshed between the two factions, and tensions are high.

How do you feel about a bit of diplomacy?

npc:252448.text: It's always great to see you, $n.

Hmm, what an odd question? Not much, I suppose. My mother used to use it as a powder for babies to prevent diaper rash, but past that, I don't know of any other good use for it.

Why do you ask?

npc:252475.text: Greetings, I am Elaadrin Evengale, the current Supreme Magister of the High Order. How can I help you?

I see. This seems dangerous in the extreme, but the situation seems to demand that risks be taken.

Very well, the High Order will provide aid. Please inform Valennia that she can count on us for this fight.

The Windshapers are almost wholly to blame for everything that has happened. Their refusal to change has damaged our ability to save ourselves from our current peril. They speak in absolutes and treat assumptions and superstitious hope as fact.

Do you know who else deals only in absolutes? The Al'Aketh. 

I for one do not intend to let blind adherence to dangerous beliefs doom our people. If it weren't for the threat of the cult, I'd march our mages over to the other side of Valanaar and wipe the Windshapers out.

npc:252476.text: It is vital that we learn more about what the cult is planning, and with the turncoat dead, the information may have died with him...

npc:252800.text: The Windfield Orchard has seen better days...

npc:253004.text: Ah, hello. You look as though you have a question for me.
Gales greetings, friend. Is there something I can help you with?
Winds tidings. What can I help you with?

npc:253066.text:
An outsider approaches me?

I doubt we have much to discuss, unless you are here to aid an old Kolkar.

npc:253372.text: <This cultist is dead. Upon close inspection, you notice that he seems to be clutching something to his chest, almost as if he was protecting it.>

npc:253471.text:
Welcome to Shen'dralas, or what remains of it.

I hope you can appreciate the majesty of this place, even if it is a haunted shell of its former self.

I'm inclined to agree. Despite our people coming together to survive the Great Sundering it seems as though the city was nonetheless doomed. How pedantic is it that its fall from grace would come from something so mundane as internal strife?

My loyalty was unquestionable in those days, but in the years since I've come to realize that the rebellion was the moment that we truly lost Prince Tortheldrin. Everything that came after is but a consequence of that wound upon his soul.
 
For my part, I try to avoid dwelling on the past, particularly my role in those events.

Try as I might though... it still haunts me.

You speak of this place by name! That is a level of respect, or knowledge, that I would not expect these days. Of the few adventurers I have encountered, most refer to the city simply as "Dire Maul".

While I find that name insulting and diminishing of my people's proud and extensive history, I cannot deny that Eldre'Thalas no longer lives up to its historical grandeur. At times I wonder if I do our city a disservice by preserving its namesake so long after it has fallen.

I hope you can excuse the state the temple and its grounds are in. So much has changed over the past few millennia.

Celebrating my own life as I stare toward the mass grave of so many of my kin feels... selfish. Many among my order remain cloistered in Prince Tortheldrin's inner sanctum, I suspect to hide from their own guilt. Seeing the city from this perspective makes it difficult to avoid painful truths.

I still count myself among the Shen'dralar, but these days I am long estranged from the library I once called home.

I suspected that my fallen brethren would be too stubborn to pass on from Eldre'Thalas completely, and assumed they would either haunt those halls for eternity or venture north to this place here to live out whatever afterlives they sought out for themselves. I painstakingly created these crystals to anchor their spirits more closely with Azeroth, allowing them to experience the world almost as though they were alive.

Indeed, it worked then. And I suspect it is working again now. I think they will be appreciative of you restoring some of their corporeality.

You should go meet them.

The full story requires time that I suspect you do not have, so I will attempt to be brief.

Perhaps the simplest way I can put it: these crystals are anchors. They can be used to permanently--well, so long as the crystals hold I suppose--bind something, someone, or even somewhere onto our plane of Azeroth. Prince Tortheldrin ordered the creation of similar pylons when he chose to bind the demon Immol'thar. Some of the Shen'dralar protested this decision and proposed a compelling alternative, but ultimately the prince was uninterested in debate and eager to silence dissent.

I had an opportunity to study their design before it became too unsafe for me to stay within the city's walls and I fled back to Shen'dralas.

The proposed alternative to demonic entanglement was at odds with what Tortheldrin had already set in motion. Given that he was working with power that tends to cloud one's judgment, it's no surprise that his first instinct was to lash out.

Most everyone who pushed back against his plans to summon and bind a demon were slain that day. Some escaped, including some of my own kin that stood in opposition to the prince, but I have yet to meet other survivors of that schism even after all these thousands of years.

npc:254151.text:
You've earned a degree of trust amongst the Nightclaw, $c. We don't have much to offer you as a reward, but we have managed to scavenge a number of crafting plans from the ruins of Ban'aethal.

The magesmiths of Ban'aethal were widely regarded to be the best artisans in all of the Skyborne Isles. The Nightclaw are naturalists, not crafters, so these records are of little use to us.

Continue to prove yourself to be a valuable ally, and I would make these secrets available to you.
The Nightclaw do not take kindly to reckless intruders. Tread carefully while in Shadowgale, $c.

npc:254345.text: Gales greetings, friend. Is there something I can help you with?

npc:254578.text:
The whole of this valley was once a garden of Eldre'Thalas, but that blighted land ahead of us was the highlight of it all. Nearly everyone contributed to its arrangement and growth. When tensions were high, often many of us would take a stroll to clear our minds.

Had it withered purely from neglect, I suspect it would look no different than the rest of Shen'dralas.

npc:254674.text:
I tended to these gardens long ago. I plucked the weeds. Trimmed the shrubbery. Planted the flowers. Alongside an elven woman, and her enchanted amulet.

Time passed. My bark aged. Weeds retaliated. Bushes wilted. Flowers withered. My branches were stiff and my movement slow, yet the elf and her people still smiled. What I could no longer do, they did in my stead.

But they stopped suddenly. This valley grew quiet. Dark. But all was well, with the elven woman's gift. Then, it was taken.

I was left with no choice. I set myself aflame. To burn it all down. So the restless weeds would not spread further.

I have died, but I still burn. The weeds still grow. I have failed.

npc:255385.text: A visitor to Shen'dralas? To what do we owe the pleasure?

npc:255894.text:
Ah, a worldly explorer!

Can you smell that fresh, ocean air? Just don't inhale too deeply. Sometimes it smells a bit fishy.

npc:255940.text: Welcome to the Calmbreeze Inn, traveler. Would you like some refreshment?

npc:256390.text: We've had trouble with shipments going missing across Azeroth. If you find any, I'd appreciate if you could return them to me.

npc:256438.text: Ah, nothing beats the smell of fresh air with a hint of sweet sap.

npc:256635.text: Adventurer! The wind bridge leading to the other spire is unstable. You may need to wait here with me until it returns.

npc:257004.text: Welcome to my shop; it's good to see another Enchanter here in Valanaar. Are you here for a lesson perhaps?
I hope that your interruption is for a good cause. I was in the middle of some important work.
Winds tidings. What can I help you with?

npc:257006.text: It appears the winds have brought you my way! I am happy to train you in the ways of cooking if you have the inclination to learn.

Cooking on Zephras may seem difficult to the untrained eye, but I enjoy the creation of every dish. Even though our dwindling home is lacking many of our traditional kaldorei ingredients, it has been fun to create new variations of the recipes of our ancestors.

I hope that no matter where the winds take you, these recipes remind you of home.

npc:257008.text: Ah, a fellow Fisherman. Are you perhaps in need of a little training? Maybe I can show you a thing or two?

npc:257036.text: Welcome to the Bank of Valanaar. We can secure your belongings and valuables here should you so desire. Do you wish to access your deposit box?

npc:257554.text: <The gaze of the ranger standing before you is fixed on the enormous anchor pylon in the distance.>

npc:257558.text:
Ah, it's been some time since we've had adventurers roam these halls. Welcome to Farholde Keep. Enjoy these comforts while you can. I'm sure you've seen the conditions we're forced to keep.

It seems every day we lose more of our home to the ever-growing infestation of Horde mongrels and Light-forsaken Twilight's Hammer cultists. With those cowards in Stormwind hiding behind their walls, we are forced to bring order to these beasts ourselves.

Perhaps you'd like to put some of those $c talents to use?

npc:257591.text: Greetings, $c. As advisor to Demar, I would be happy to answer any questions you have about Farholde Keep.

npc:257595.text: Welcome to my Inn, weary traveler. What can I do for you?
Are you interested in exploring one of these dungeons?

npc:258130.text:
<Before you lies the corpse of Jorel Windsinger.

Deep lacerations are cut into his legs, and lightning burns scorch his fur.

It is clear he put up a fight before succumbing to his wounds.>

npc:259012.text: All of the skyborne islands became destabilized and began to move apart a few years ago. If that wasn't bad enough, now large pieces of Zephras are beginning to fall away. It's hard to imagine your home falling into the sky, but that is my reality now.

npc:259013.text:
<Before you lies a skyborne; his body is mangled and bruised but still recognizable. It is clear he met a gruesome end while attempting to flee.

It appears that all of his belongings are still on his body, and a half-filled crate nearby lies spilled on the ground.>

npc:260568.text:
No fights goin' on today, pal. The Horde and the Alliance are too busy killin' each other out in the fields when there's perfectly good coin to be made doin' that in my arena! Go figure.

Come back when I get this place up and runnin'.

npc:263113.text: It can get boring up here, you know. I can only annoy that stuffy wretch Halaan so much before even that gets old.

npc:263120.text:
What the hell do you want? Can't you see I'm busy here?

Why don't you make yourself useful and have Zizplink pour me another drink. Mine's running dry.

npc:275269.text: Board here for transport to Dalaran City, nestled in the Alterac Mountains.

npc:276316.text:
If ye want to see the elven port of Auberdine and all its mysterious mist, you've come to the right dock. If ye also want to see the beauty and glory of Menethil Harbor, even better--same ship'll take ye there, too!

It ain't a journey for the weak, but if you've got the spirit of adventure in yer gullet then yer in luck!

npc:295.text: Welcome to my Inn, weary traveler. What can I do for you?

npc:3179.text: I can teach you fishing skills.

npc:3309.text: Would you rather trust your goods with a goblin?
Besides the Grunts outside, my brothers and I fought at the battle of Hyjal. Any who seek to steal from the bank must face us first.

npc:3310.text: You haven't lived until you've looked down on the world from the back of a wind rider.

npc:3318.text: Would you rather trust your goods with a goblin?

npc:3320.text: Besides the Grunts outside, my brothers and I fought at the battle of Hyjal. Any who seek to steal from the bank must face us first.
I guarantee this bank's security with my own blood, is that good enough for you?

npc:3332.text: Fish so delicious. You come learn fish? Eat fish? Mmmmm...

npc:3354.text: Are you here for training?  Or are you just here to waste a warrior's time.

Through rigorous retraining I have had to break many students of all they had previously learned so that I might teach them anew.  The service I offer becomes increasingly difficult to perform each time it is done.  It is for that reason that it becomes increasingly expensive with each retraining.  Do you desire that I break you of the talents you have learned?

npc:3615.text: My wind riders are trained to fly quickly through the hot Barrens air.

npc:4312.text: Where would you like to fly to?

npc:4551.text: How may I be of service?

npc:4556.text: Greetings, and welcome.  I am not very good at smiling, but trust me; I am happy to serve you.

npc:459.text: The arcane only corrupts those who are weak. Even if you do not follow the path of the warlock, you would do well to remember that.

npc:4591.text: I can train you in First Aid techniques.

npc:4616.text: If I wasn't stuck here day in and day out, I would have attained the mastery required to train the likes of you! Unfortunately that's not the case. Go talk to Hgarth at the Sun Rock Retreat in the Stonetalon Mountains.

npc:5396.text: The Alliance has many stakes in Desolace, and our hold here is unstable.$B$BWill you help us?

npc:5411.text: Welcome to Tanaris, $n. How can I be of service to you today? You don't look like a blacksmith to me, but I know how looks can be deceiving.

npc:5594.text: In need of some alchemy supplies, are we?  Or do you have other business with me?

npc:5883.text: Greetings, $c.  Are you here to learn of the hidden arts?

npc:6373.text: Want to make your demons more powerful?  It'll cost you, but you've come to the right place.

npc:6374.text: Want to make your demons more powerful?  It'll cost you, but you've come to the right place.

npc:6491.text: It is not yet your time. I shall aid your journey back to the realm of the living... for a price.

npc:6546.text: Your errand must mean much, $c, to draw you so deep into the marsh...

npc:6740.text: Welcome to my Inn, weary traveler. What can I do for you?

npc:6929.text: If we are to make these new lands ours then we must have places to rest our battle weary bodies. Lay your axe by the fire and share the stories of your mighty battles.

npc:7010.text: These are dangerous times, skyborne.  An ancient evil is rising, and it cares not if you're Horde or Alliance.

npc:716.text: Master Nesingwary has a big hunt ahead of him.  I find helping him prepare for a day in the jungle is much more relaxing than helping him ready for combat.  Although I do miss some of those glorious moments on the battlefield.

npc:7406.text: Hello there $glad:lass;... the name's Oglethorpe and I may be responsible for one of the amazing gnomish devices you might possess!  If it blew up, then it wasn't me; if it made you rich though, we can discuss royalties!$B$BOh, and if you're from Gnomeregan, you can just take two ninety degree angles, smash them together, and start marching.  I have nothing to say to you.
Well, if it isn't $n!  It's good to see you again; I cannot express my gratitude enough at the help that you've given me and my invention work to date.$B$BWhat can I do for you today?

npc:7564.text: Living out here in the desert is rough! I get so thirsty standing outside in this heat.

npc:7683.text: Welcome to Blue Moon Odds and Ends, $c.  If you have any questions, please let me know.

npc:7763.text: Hi there! I have a proposition for an adventure-seeker such as you, if you are up to the challenge!$B$BAlong with my invention, the Super Egg-O-Matic, I am hard at work aiding the druids with their campaign to save the hippogryphs. The birds are being affected by the evil effects of the Gordunni ogres inhabiting the ruins of Feralas, and their numbers are dwindling.$B$BI collect many different types of eggs.  Will you help and find some for me?

npc:7771.text: I know, I know, I'm out here in the middle of nowhere!$B$BMy home is actually in Ratchet, but after crashing my zeppelin here, I thought I might as well start the research I came here to do!

npc:7776.text: Listen to the stories of an elder. $n. I have many to speak of...

npc:7937.text: Hello there, $c. I am High Tinker Mekkatorque of the exiles of Gnomeregan.

npc:8496.text: Hi there. No, Marvon sure isn't here, and he won't be back for quite some time. Actually, I am getting a little worried about him...$B$BI hope he gets back soon. A large chest arrived for him and it's too heavy for me to lug it inside here! I had to leave it out by the door...

npc:8587.text: I am not here because of honor, $n. I am here because of one orc's pride.$B$BIf I had not rejected Belgrom's offers, then I'm sure I'd still be in Orgrimmar taking care of real business.$B$BHis debauchery is no secret to the female warriors in Durotar, but that certainly doesn't stop him from being his charming self.$B$BHe's lucky he didn't pursue his desire for me much longer though--he'd be short more than just the digits on his hands.

npc:906.text: The arcane only corrupts those who are weak. Keep up on your training, or you may find a similar fate.

npc:11039.text: Greetings, $N. I am Duke Nicholas Zverenhoff of the Argent Dawn.

npc:1239.text: If you're willing to endure tales that will shiver your timbers and sog your skivvies, then get yourself a drink and sit for a spell...

npc:1480.text: Alchemy can help so many people! It's my life's passion.

npc:2094.text: Greetings, $c. I'm in a bit of a pinch right now, running very low on hides.

npc:240.text: Ach, it's hard enough keeping order around here without all these new troubles popping up! I hope you have good news, $N...

npc:241.text: Hey there, friend.  My name's Remy.  I'm from Redridge to the east, and came here looking for business, looking for business.  You got any...got any??

npc:253.text: Aha!  Good day, good day, Master $C!  Come, sit down and have a drink.  You have an enterprising look in your eye, and I think you'll find speaking to me worth your time...

npc:257944.text: I cannot believe we were taken by surprise by the Al'Aketh. They have never been hostile to us before, but with their ambush they injured many of my kin. I swear I will get revenge for the fallen and wounded druids of my den. Mark my words, they will pay.

npc:258023.text: If you want something done right, you send me to do it.

npc:259352.text: Whatever you want, spit it out already. I've got a long shift ahead of me.

npc:259961.text: Lemme tell ya, kid. It ain't easy bein' a wharfmaster. If you heard all the logistics involved in gettin' something as simple as a crate of apples shipped across the sea, it'd make your head spin.

npc:259962.text: Please, grab any open chair ya like. I'll come take your order in a sec.

npc:5204.text: If we are to make our place in this world, then we will do so through study, and through the will to ignore our fading human instincts.

npc:7876.text: Some people wonder what we're doing out here in the desert.  Well... if I told you, then you'd stay and try to make our profits!

npc:7882.text: We're here to make a profit.  And having our goods stolen is no way to make a profit.

npc:823.text: Hello there, $c.  Normally I'd be out on the beat looking after the folk of Stormwind, but a lot of the Stormwind guards are fighting in other lands.  So here I am, deputized and offering bounties when I'd rather be on patrol...

meta.attribution: Data from Efficient Games (https://efficient.games), licensed under CC BY 4.0.

accept.text: Garrick Padfoot - a cutthroat who's plagued our farmers and merchants for weeks - was seen at a shack near the vineyards, which lies east of the Abbey and across the bridge.  Bring me the villain's head, and earn his bounty!$B$BBut be wary, $n.  Garrick has gathered a gang of thugs around him.  He will not be an easy man to reach.

complete.text: Hah - you caught him!  You've done Elwynn a great service, and earned a nice bounty!

objectives.text: Kill Garrick Padfoot and bring his head to Deputy Willem at Northshire Abbey.

progress.text: Did you find Garrick's shack?  Are we finally free of that villain?

accept.text: Your first task is one of cleansing, $n.  A clan of kobolds have infested the woods to the north.  Go there and fight the kobold vermin you find.  Reduce their numbers so that we may one day drive them from Northshire.

complete.text:
Well done, citizen.  Those kobolds are thieves and cowards, but in large numbers they pose a threat to us.  And the humans of Stormwind do not need another threat.

For defeating them, you have my gratitude.

objectives.text: Kill 10 Kobold Vermin, then return to Marshal McBride.

accept.text: Oh, this is just terrible!  I sent out my top assistant, Junior Surveyor Scrimshank, into the desert southeast of here.  That's an area we call the Gaping Chasm.  Well, he's gone missing, and his last report had more of those weird bugs where he was.  Could it be that they've infested two major regions of the desert now?$B$BI need you to head into the Gaping Chasm and look for Scrimshank, please!  That... or at least find his surveying equipment.  I fear that may be all that is left of the poor sod.

complete.text:
He was a good goblin, young Scrimshank.  Let's hope that his demise was not in vain by what he was able to record with his surveying equipment.

It seems as though we have quite the situation on our hands here with these bugs.  They're way too cunning for their own good, and the research we've done so far is shaping up to indicate that they might even be under the controlling influence of a third party!  If this is the case, then it bodes ill for not only Gadgetzan, but the whole desert!

objectives.text: Discover the fate of Junior Surveyor Scrimshank, and bring either him or his surveying equipment to Senior Surveyor Fizzledowser in Gadgetzan.

progress.text: Well, what news do you have?  You look like you've been in quite the fight... is Scrimshank alive?

accept.text: $n, my scouts tell me that the kobold infestation is larger than we had thought.  A group of kobold workers has camped near the Echo Ridge Mine to the north.$B$BGo to the mine and remove them.  We know there are at least 10.  Kill them, see if there are more, then report back to me.

complete.text: I don't like hearing of all these kobolds in our mine.  No good can come of this.  Here, take this as payment, and when you're ready, speak to me again.  I would like you to go back to the mines one more time...

objectives.text: Kill 10 Kobold Workers, then report back to Marshal McBride.

accept.text: Recently, a new group of thieves has been hanging around Northshire.  They call themselves the Defias Brotherhood, and have been seen across the river to the east.$B$BI don't know what they're up to, but I'm sure it's not good!  Bring me the bandanas they wear, and I'll reward you with a weapon.

complete.text: Back with some bandanas, I see.  The Stormwind Army appreciates your help.

objectives.text: Bring 12 Red Burlap Bandanas to Deputy Willem outside the Northshire Abbey.

progress.text: Have you gathered those bandanas for me yet?

accept.text: Your previous investigations are proof that the Echo Ridge Mine needs purging.  Return to the mine and help clear it of kobolds.$B$BWaste no time, $n.  The longer the kobolds are left unmolested in the mine, the deeper a foothold they gain in Northshire.

complete.text: Once again, you have earned my respect, and the gratitude of the Stormwind Army.  There may yet be kobolds in the mine, but I will marshal others against them.  We have further tasks for you.

objectives.text: Kill 12 Kobold Laborers, then return to Marshal McBride at Northshire Abbey.

accept.text: Here's your report.  I urge you to take it to someone who might have working knowledge in this kind of thing.$B$BI know this troll scholar named Zilzibin Drumlore.  He's spent a lot of time studying life forms that are unique to the ecology of Azeroth; he's a historian to boot!  If you want someone to help figure out what exactly this threat is and how to stop it, give this report to him.  We're going to need all the help we can get.$B$BZil lives in a house on the second tier of the Drag in Orgrimmar.

complete.text:
This report... I've dealt with these beasts before.  Fizzledowser was wise to send this, and you, to me.

These creatures will consume the Tanaris desert rapidly; they are nothing short of one of the greatest menaces we all will ever face.  Familiarize yourself with this name, $N: silithid.  The insects mentioned here are the silithid, and they are the tools of one of the greatest threats that both the Horde and Alliance face.

If only we were smart enough to see that before.

objectives.text: Take the report to Zilzibin Drumlore in Orgrimmar.

progress.text: I'm sorry, I don't know you... but from the look of things you have at least heard something of me.  Now, what can I help you with?  Do you have something for me?

accept.text: I hate those nasty timber wolves!  But I sure like eating wolf steaks...  Bring me tough wolf meat and I will exchange it for something you'll find useful.$B$BTough wolf meat is gathered from hunting the timber wolves and young wolves wandering the Northshire countryside.

complete.text:
You've been busy!  I can't wait to cook up that wolf meat...

I have some things here you might want - take your pick!

objectives.text: Bring 8 pieces of Tough Wolf Meat to Eagan Peltskinner outside Northshire Abbey.

progress.text: Hey $N.  I'm getting hungry...did you get that tough wolf meat?

accept.text: If you are concerned that the rumors of murlocs are true, then do this -- travel to the eastern Elwynn bridge and speak with Guard Thomas.  He has been stationed at the bridge for the past week and will know the state of the area.$B$BBring me his report.

objectives.text: Marshal Dughan wants you to speak with Guard Thomas.

accept.text: $n, there's a new threat in Elwynn Forest!  Murlocs are swimming up the streams of eastern Elwynn, scaring away fish and attacking gentle folk!$B$BI warned Marshal Dughan, but he's more worried about the gnolls and the bandits.  He's not convinced that the murlocs are a danger.$B$BPlease, $n, speak to Dughan and persuade him to send more troops to the east!

complete.text:
Yes, I spoke with Remy.  I respect him as a merchant, though all reports of Murlocs to the east have been sketchy at best.

Your concerns are noted, but unless I receive a military report of a murloc threat, we can't afford to send more troops east.

objectives.text: Remy "Two Times" wants you to speak with Marshal Dughan in Goldshire.

accept.text: The Kobolds in these parts sometimes carry Gold Dust on them.  I could really use the stuff - bring me a load of it and I'll give you the best price in town...best price in town!$B$BYou can find kobolds in the Fargodeep Mine to the south, and around the Jasperlode Mine to the northeast.

objectives.text: Bring 10 Gold Dust to Remy "Two Times" in Goldshire.  Gold Dust is gathered from Kobolds in Elwynn Forest.

accept.text: $n, you are a $c with proven interest in the security of Northshire.  You are now tasked with the protection of the surrounding Elwynn Forest.$B$BIf you accept this duty, then I have prepared papers that must be delivered to Marshal Dughan in Goldshire.  Goldshire lies along the southern road, past the border gates.

complete.text:
Well, it says here that you've been awarded Acting Deputy Status with the Stormwind Marshals.  Congratulations.

And good luck - keeping Elwynn safe is no picnic... what with most the army busy doing who knows what for who knows which noble!

It's hard to keep track of politics in these dark days...

objectives.text: Take Marshal McBride's Documents to Marshal Dughan in Goldshire.

progress.text:
You have word from McBride?  Northshire is a garden compared to Elwynn Forest, but I wonder what Marshal McBride has to report.

Here, let me have his papers...

accept.text: Hello, $ggood sir:my lady;!  Do you have a moment?$B$BMy brother and I run an apothecary in Stormwind, and I'm here to gather large candles for their wax.  Can you help me?$B$BYou can get large candles from kobolds, and I hear rumors that kobolds are infesting the Elwynn mines ... the Fargodeep mine to the south and Jasperlode Mine to the east.  I suggest looking for candles in one of those places.

complete.text: You were busy hunting kobolds, were you?  Thanks for the candles, $N, and here's your reward...

objectives.text: Bring 8 Large Candles to William Pestle in Goldshire.

progress.text: Did you gather those candles yet?

accept.text: My brother Morgan is waiting in Stormwind for my shipment of candles.  I don't have enough time to make the trip myself, but if you'd like to take him the shipment, he'll pay you well.$B$BI've packed up the candles, and you can find Morgan in our shop, Pestle's Apothecary, in the Stormwind Trade District.

objectives.text: Bring William's Shipment to Morgan Pestle in the Stormwind Trade District.

accept.text: The mine in Northshire isn't the only one with problems!  I have reports that the Fargodeep Mine in Elwynn has also become a haven for Kobolds.$B$BExplore the mine and confirm these reports, then return to me.  The mine is almost due south of Goldshire, between the Stonefield and Maclure homesteads.

complete.text: This is bad news.  What's next, dragons?!?  We'll have to increase our patrols near that mine.  Thanks for your efforts, $N.  And hold a moment... I might have another task for you.

objectives.text: Explore the Fargodeep Mine, then return to Marshal Dughan in Goldshire.

accept.text: Thanks to you we know the Fargodeep Mine is infested with kobolds.  Now we need a scout to investigate the more distant Jasperlode Mine.$B$BExplore Jasperlode and confirm any kobold presence.  To reach the mine, travel east along the road until you reach the Tower of Azora.  From the tower, head north and you'll find the mine in the foothills.

objectives.text: Explore the Jasperlode Mine, then report back to Marshal Dughan in Goldshire.

accept.text: I possess original packaging materials for the ripple Dran Droffers seeks.  I will assist you in packaging the ripple for Malton's abrasive father... for a fee of two additional bottles of said ripple.  They are located in crates found in the abandoned Horde base near Skulk Rock.$B$BIt will be an arduous task, to wit; foul slimes and oozes will be found sticking to the ruins; rumor has it they are led by some sort of master ooze.  Regardless, procure the ripple and return to me here for packaging.

objectives.text: Recover 10 bottles of Hinterlands Honey Ripple from the crates located around the abandoned Horde base in Skulk Rock.

complete.text:
Good work - I'll start my analysis on these now!  I can tell you right from the start though... these are nothing like any insect form I have ever seen.  It's almost as if these bugs are being controlled by an outside force or something.

You need to go talk to Fizzledowser right away; apparently there is an emergency that he needs your help with on the double!  I'm not sure, but I think it involves more of the bugs in the Tanaris desert!

progress.text: You're Junior Surveyor $N, yes?  Quickly now, there is a dire situation at hand!  Do you have the insect parts that Fizzledowser said you would?!

accept.text: I lost my necklace, and think that guttersnipe Billy Maclure took it!  He's usually scuttling like a rat around the Maclure vineyards east of here. $B$BGet my necklace back for me, and you'll warm an old widow's heart.

complete.text:
You lost a what?  Well I didn't take no necklace, because I ain't no thief!

I might know who did but...<grin>...I'm too hungry to remember.

objectives.text: Speak with Billy Maclure.

accept.text: Maybe if I got a pie, I could tell you who has that necklace.  And you know, I think that old Bernice lady at that other farm makes great Pork Belly Pies... $B$BMaybe if you gave her some chunks of boar meat from the boars that hang around our farms, and told her what it was for, she'd bake up a pie for you.

objectives.text: Bring 4 Chunks of Boar Meat to Auntie Bernice Stonefield at the Stonefield's Farm.

accept.text: The Brackwells have a prize-winning pig, Princess.  The sow is HUGE, and she got that way from sneaking over here and eating my veggies!$B$BSo before she comes to our fields...Princess must die!  Bring me her collar as proof of the deed and I'll give you something for your time!$B$BPrincess is usually over at the Brackwell Pumpkin Patch, to the east and beyond the Maclure farm.  Get her before she gets hungry and comes back here!

objectives.text: Kill Princess, grab her collar, then bring it back to Ma Stonefield at the Stonefield Farm.

accept.text: Oh, I'm cursed!  My heart belongs to Tommy Joe Stonefield, but our families are bitter enemies.  So I can't see him, even though my eyes ache to gaze upon that handsome face!$B$BPlease, take this letter and give it to Tommy Joe.  He's usually at the river to the west of the Stonefield Farm, which is due west of here.

complete.text: Ah!  I can't stand us being apart.  I have to see her!!

objectives.text: Give Maybell's Love Letter to Tommy Joe Stonefield.

progress.text: You have what??  Maybell is the light of my dull life.  Hurry, let me see her letter!

accept.text: I bet William Pestle has a potion to unite our two young lovers!$B$BHere, take this note to William.  He's staying at the Lion's Pride Inn in Goldshire.

complete.text:
My heart goes out to those two poor souls, Maybell and Tommy Joe.  I remember being young and in love, once.

There must be something I can do to help them!  Let me think...

objectives.text: Take Gramma Stonefield's Note to William Pestle.

progress.text: You have a note from "Gramma" Stonefield, eh?  I haven't seen Mildred in years!  I wonder what she has to say...

accept.text: I'm going to spend some time taking a look at Scrimshank's surveying gear... as well as putting his personal effects in order.  I get the sneaking feeling behind my ears that this isn't the last loss we'll be facing against these bugs.$B$BI'd like for you to check in with Alchemist Pestlezugg to see if he has had a chance to process the insect parts we sent him.  If they're ready, bring them to me.

complete.text:
